paper_metadata.title: Improving the Sequence Alignment Method by Quantum Multi-Pattern Recognition

experiments.description: A conceptual/hypothetical application of quantum multi-pattern recognition to pairwise sequence alignment using dot-matrix diagonals as patterns, illustrated on the XL23808 vs XLRHODOP DNA dot plot. The paper describes dividing the vertical sequence into 50-digit fragments and running the recognition procedure repeatedly to identify matching diagonal regions.

algorithm.variant: Quantum multi-pattern recognition adapted from Zhou and Ding's Grover-like search

hyperparameters.success_probability_claim: 100% when recognized patterns exceed 1/3 of total patterns

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial quantum state |φ0⟩ formed by learning the pattern set P and spurious set S

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each full diagonal of the dot matrix is treated as a one-dimensional binary vector dataset; the smaller sequence is split into fragments and each fragment is compared against diagonal datasets.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Identify matching diagonal regions in a dot-matrix representation of pairwise sequence alignment.

problem_instance.description: Pairwise DNA sequence alignment on the dot plot of XL23808 (horizontal) and XLRHODOP (vertical), with the vertical sequence divided into 50-digit pieces.
problem_instance.dataset_name: European Molecular Biology Laboratory DNA sequences

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Dot-matrix plot construction; shorter diagonal regions padded to equalize length; vertical sequence split into 50-digit fragments.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct dot-matrix recurrence plot; encode each diagonal as a binary vector; pad shorter diagonals; split the long sequence into fragments.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical methods may assemble the final alignment from detected diagonals; local SA can be applied after locating similar regions.

speedup_claims.factor: O(sqrt(N/n)) per search; approximately 1 iteration per 50-digit fragment in the example
speedup_claims.conditions: when the learning pattern set is over 1/3 of the total patterns; example uses 50-digit fragments and about 32 search applications
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper is conceptual and does not provide an empirical runtime benchmark; the claimed 100% probability depends on the >1/3 pattern fraction condition.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial-time speedup over O(s1.s2) classical alignment
speedup_claims.conditions: pairwise sequence alignment using dot-matrix diagonal recognition
speedup_claims.caveats: No measured wall-clock times are reported; the claim is based on algorithmic complexity and a worked example.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N/n)) per search iteration count; repeated about 32 times in the example
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: more than 7.2×10^6 computing steps (as stated for the example)
